newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products up, gas oil premiums pressured.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products up, gas oil premiums pressured.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were firmer on Monday but gas oil premiums were under pressure from increased supply, traders said.
Gasoline was firm, and one major Italian refiner, sold out until mid-November, was considering boosting gasoline runs at the expense of naphtha.
"We have had several enquiries for prompt cargoes...We are meeting with our operations manager to see if we will push the refinery to produce gasoline," the refiner said.
If they decide to sell the price would be around fob quotes high +$2 a tonne, fob Italian islands.
Traders were divided on naphtha. Some said it was softer with arbitrage opportunities to the Far East and the U.S. keeping the market well-supplied.
But a Suez cargo, already on the water, was seen offered at $227 in NWE, translating to a firm $223/$224 cif Med.
"I think the belief is that things were overdone to the downside last week," said one broker.

Gas oil firmed on futures but physical trade was thin and margins looked under pressure. Traders said lack of a vessel blocked efforts by three players to cover a tender for 125,000 tonnes of 0.5 percent sulphur material into Turkey in November.

Another supplier offered 35,000 tonnes of Russian from Tuapse at high fob quotes +$0.50 loading Nov 2/3, ideal for delivery of two Turkish cargoes scheduled for Nov 5-9. The bid was fob quotes high -$0.50.

Fuel oil was boosted by a Turkish tender to buy 25-50,000 tonnes of high sulphur and 55-60,000 tonnes of low sulphur, for delivery into Aliaga, Izmit and Tutunciftlik around mid Nov. The high sulphur tender was said unusual, as Turkey normally exports it. Officials at utility Tupras were not available for comment.
An Italian refiner was heard having bought a 25,000 tonne low sulphur Russian cargo, originating in Novorisiisk.
